claims.text: Containerless electromagnetic levitation coupled with high-resolution DSC and in-situ dilatometry enables more accurate melting-property measurements for equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi than traditional crucible-based methods.
The initial alloy is homogeneous, solid, and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
High-purity inert gas or vacuum minimizes contamination during measurement.
Heating rates of 10–50 K/min provide near-equilibrium conditions during the solid-to-liquid transition.
Eliminating crucible interactions suppresses heterogeneous nucleation.
Suppressing heterogeneous nucleation and contamination produces a clearer and more precise thermal event.
DSC heat-flow measurements capture the alloy's melting event.
Simultaneous in-situ dilatometry captures the volume change at melting.
Combining reduced extrinsic effects, DSC heat flow, and dilatometry permits high-fidelity extraction of melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting volume change.
The proposed method will determine melting temperature with an error within ±2%.
The proposed method will determine fusion enthalpy and entropy with errors within ±5%.
The proposed method will determine the volume change at melting with an error within ±5%.
The proposed method will significantly improve precision relative to crucible-based measurements.
Traditional crucible-based DSC suffers from contamination and heterogeneous-nucleation effects that reduce accuracy.
Applicability to HEA compositions beyond equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi may require additional calibration and validation.
Failure to reduce measurement uncertainty by at least 50% relative to crucible-based DSC, or failure to extract the thermodynamic parameters reliably, would falsify the proposed method.
